journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Protection," says Moth, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: Two drunks, a stolen goose and a lost dog. The dog was the most reasonable of them. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 2 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Piet Wieland has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: A Sighting
journal.text: Moth has seen Bartel Holzschuher. "Same tavern every night. Ask me how I know."

journal.title: Cleared: Hodge Kessler
journal.text: You try Hodge Kessler's story. It holds: a night at the Harbour crane with a dozen porters. Strike one name from the casebook.

journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Not Guilty: Bartel Holzschuher
journal.text: The sworn men acquit. Bartel Holzschuher walks down the court steps into the crowd's cheering and looks straight at you.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Kuiper the Goldsmith's
journal.text: Regina Holzschuher is not sure when it happened: some time between Friday night and Monday morning. Only the study casement was touched, and only the deeds and the coin taken. A neighbour reports seeing a light in the study past compline. Somebody knew the house. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: You sit. You listen. You let the silence do the work. Eventually the Tiler says: "They stuck on their words. K-k-, like that."

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: An Insight: The Fencing-master
journal.text: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Taken: Bartel Holzschuher
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: The Cough Clears
journal.text: Bitter bark in wine, two days sweating under every blanket you own, and on the third morning the river smells like a river again.

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour: Keep the file
journal.text: The clerk's smile does not reach his eyes. Your name is spoken in the chamber, not warmly, and in the lanes, warmly. (Standing rises)

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour
journal.text: The Council's clerk lingers after delivering the stipend. A councillor's son was found where he should not have been, with people he should not have known. There is a file. It would be a kindness if there were not. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Nothing Doing
journal.text: You walk until your feet hurt. The city keeps its secrets. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Sickness
journal.text: A cough from the river, a heat behind the eyes. The Warrens give it to everyone in the end. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Apothecary's Key, you only get part of it. The apothecary recovers the columns. They do not add up, and somebody knew they would not. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Bartel Holzschuher Cracks
journal.text: You lay The Inventory on the table and say nothing. Bartel Holzschuher stares at it for a long time. Then they start to talk.

journal.title: Ahead of the Crier
journal.text: "Something is going to happen," says Moth. "Soon." Keep the warning on the table: when it comes, you will be ready for it.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Aeltje Kempe walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over a Tenement in de Witt Row. You find: A second set of books.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at a Tenement in de Witt Row. You find: Convenient Losses, What the Child Heard, The Smell Under the Smoke. The first name in the casebook: Hodge Kessler. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Bartel Holzschuher, a nephew of the house. It has to be.

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: A gentle question, then another. Bartel Holzschuher is angry about something, and it comes out sideways. The nephew was cut out of the will a week ago, loudly, at table.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. The fire at a Tenement in de Witt Row after the guild's audit was announced destroyed exactly what somebody needed destroyed: the strongbox was empty and unmelted. Everything else survived. Including, in a drawer nobody checked, a second set of books.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Fletcher's Pawnshop. You find: Disturbed Dust, A Key, Not a Crow. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Margery Imhoff.

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother: Give him the week, and his wage
journal.text: He goes. The others see it. (Standing rises; Dread eases)

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother
journal.text: One of your watchmen asks for the week: his mother is dying in the Warrens and there is nobody else. The round will be short a man. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Watch who leaves
journal.text: You let it burn out and watch the door. The potboy sees you watching, and sees a living in it. (An Informer at the Swan)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Aeltje Kempe takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: The Letter of Appointment
journal.text: The Council's seal is still warm on the letter that makes you Examiner. The Burgomaster's chamber is up one flight and has a window; yours is under the stair and has a case on it already. Everyone in the Watch-house knows which one you are looking at.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop
journal.text: No broken glass at Anneke Barker's. Whoever came in on the one evening the shop shuts early used the front door, with a key, and left with three silver spoons and a ledger. A neighbour reports seeing a familiar cloak in the doorway.
